title: I have ~3 years of NQ order flow + order book data (tick-by-tick, aggressor side, L2). Send me your strategy and I'll backtest it for free
author: x-sForky
selftext:
I spent the last weeks building an order-flow dataset for NQ (E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures) and testing my own ideas on it. Most of them died, so I'd rather put the data to work: \*\*if you have an order-flow or order-book strategy you've always wanted to test properly, send me the rules and I'll run it and share the results with you. Free.\*\*

\*\*What the data is\*\*

\- \*\*Period:\*\* Sep 7, 2023 → Jul 10, 2026 (735 trading days, full Globex sessions)  
\- \*\*Trades:\*\* every single trade with its aggressor side (buy/sell). Checked 100% identical against NinjaTrader's tape on overlapping days.  
\- \*\*Order book:\*\* full market depth by price level (L2 updates for bids and asks, plus best bid/ask). Validated against Databento MBP-10: per-minute top-10 depth correlation 0.96–0.99.  
\- \*\*Bonus:\*\* \~65 days (Jul–Oct 2026) of NinjaTrader market-replay L2.

\*\*Size\*\*

\- Raw book + trades: \*\*83 GB compressed\*\* (\~12 million events per day)  
\- Tick tape (trades with side, bid/ask): \*\*45 GB\*\*  
\- Market-replay L2: \*\*10 GB\*\*  
\- Per-minute book features (imbalance, depth, walls, spread): 219 MB

\*\*What I can test for you\*\*

\- Order-flow signals: delta, CVD divergence, absorption, imbalances, big trades, footprint patterns, effort vs. result…  
\- Book-based filters on an existing strategy: imbalance, depth, walls/"icebergs", spread at entry  
\- Fill realism: does your limit order really fill when price just \*touches\* it, or does it need to trade through? What's your real slippage on market entries?

\*\*What I need from you\*\*

Mechanical rules (entry, stop, target, timeframe, session), or Python code. Discretionary "you'll see it on the chart" setups can't be backtested, sorry.

\*\*What you get\*\*

Trade list + stats (win rate, R per trade, profit factor, drawdown, by year), with realistic costs, and an honest split between in-sample and out-of-sample periods.

\*\*Fair warning (and why I'm posting this)\*\*

I tested \~80 order-flow and order-book hypotheses on this data with pre-registered rules and out-of-sample checks: absorption, zero prints, delta outliers, CVD divergence, effort vs. result, book imbalance, depth, walls, iceberg detection, closing flow… \*\*None survived out of sample after costs.\*\* Several looked great in one year and flipped sign in the next. Maybe your idea is the exception. I'd genuinely like to find one that works.

\*\*I can't share or sell the raw data\*\* (exchange licensing), only the results of the tests.

Drop a comment or DM me with your rules.
